title: Exclusive: Amazon Web Services CFO says AI spending is sustainable
key_facts: AWS chief financial officer John Felton told Axios that the boom in AI infrastructure and services spending is sustainable because it drives meaningful innovation.
He said AWS's AI server investments pay back in under three years and that AWS had a nearly $500 billion order backlog as of the second quarter.
AWS posted second-quarter revenue of $42.2 billion, up 36.7% from a year earlier; its AI revenue run rate was over $25 billion and growing at a triple-digit percentage rate.

His comments came after Gartner estimated that more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could be exposed to impairment by the end of 2030 and projected that more than 80% of specialised AI cloud providers will cease operating independently by 2030.
Axios notes AWS is exposed to the risks but is among the companies best positioned to withstand them.
Felton said he was surprised by the anti-data-center movement and that data centers have 30-year useful lives.
quote_evidence: The boom in spending on AI infrastructure and services is sustainable because it's driving meaningful innovation, the CFO of Amazon Web Services tells Axios.
He also says AWS' AI server investments are proving fruitful: "We're seeing paybacks of under three years on those servers."

The big picture: His comments came after Gartner research analysts rattled investors with a report estimating that more than $3.5 trillion in AI infrastructure spending "could be exposed to impairment" by the end of 2030.
why_it_matters_hint: AWS's finance chief says AI spending is paying back, in answer to bubble worries after a Gartner warning, but the figures are the company's own.
event_date: 16 Oct 2026 (Yahoo Finance's article date; the interview date is not stated)
notes: Read on Yahoo Finance, which carries Axios's own text ('tells Axios', Axios AI+ footer); the original Axios link was not given, so the Yahoo page is the url. REPLY-STYLE: answers a Gartner report of Wednesday 14 Oct; our 15 Oct edition carried a different Gartner forecast, about neocloud companies.
